attempts.summary: Formed a 3-node RabbitMQ 3.5.7 cluster (node1, node2, node3, all disc nodes, shared Erlang cookie) on Ubuntu 16.04. Created the `payments` vhost with an `app_user` account granted full permissions, and an `ha-all` mirroring policy (ha-mode=all, ha-sync-mode=automatic) so all queues in the vhost mirror to every node. Declared a durable queue `orders`, published a persistent message, and proved survival of node loss: stopped node1 (then the queue master), confirmed the queue promoted to node3 with the message intact, and successfully consumed it from node2. Restarted node1, confirmed full resync. Then performed the mandatory sequential reboot of all three nodes (one at a time, native `shutdown -r now`), capturing pre/post boot_id changes for each and confirming RabbitMQ came back active, rejoined the cluster with zero partitions, and the queue was fully synchronised with the message preserved after each restart.
